top_story: Iran’s drone strike on a US base in Bahrain on 15 November sharply raised the risk of direct US-Iran escalation and further narrowed space for any renewed diplomacy, prompting top-level crisis management at a trilateral Trump-Putin-Xi summit in China later that day. The summit reflects how the Iran war is now reorganizing great-power coordination well beyond the Gulf, as Washington’s security posture, Moscow’s balancing role, and Beijing’s regional stakes increasingly intersect. On 16 November, disclosure that the Israeli military had uploaded 3.5 million photos to Amazon’s facial recognition platform during the Gaza bombardment underscored a parallel hardening of coercive control over Palestinians, extending the war’s impact from physical devastation into mass digital surveillance. Taken together, these developments show a regional conflict deepening on two tracks: widening interstate confrontation around Iran and more entrenched systems of domination shaping Palestinian civilian life.
